examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ταῦτα τοὺς πολλοὺς καὶ φαύλους περὶ αὐτοῦ πεποίηκε λέγοντας.
examples.translation: Thus he represents the multitude and men of low degree as speaking of him.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Τοῖς μὲν δὴ μὴ παροῦσιν οὕτω προσεφέρετο·

examples.original: Οὐ μὴν ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ τῶν παρόντων ἀναλαμβάνειν ἐπειρᾶτο τὴν πόλιν.
examples.translation: However, as far as circumstances allowed, he endeavoured to restore the city.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.translation: When they had thus talked things over together, they came to an agreement according to this last suggestion and proceeded to act upon it.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Τούτῳ μὲν οὕτως εἶπε, καὶ δοὺς τὴν ἐπιστολὴν ἀπέπεμπε, προσεντειλάμενος οὕτω σπεύδειν ὥσπερ οἶδεν ὅτι συμφέρει ταχὺ παρεῖναι.

examples.translation: Do your senses tell you that you are awake?
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Τῇδε· ὁ μὲν ὁρῶν ἐπιστήμων, φαμέν, τούτου γέγονεν οὗπερ ὁρῶν·
examples.translation: This is how it is: he who sees has acquired knowledge, we say, of that which he has seen;

examples.author: Plutarch

examples.translation: On the other hand the destruction which oil causes is due rather to a kind of addition than to removal;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.translation: Now, to recount the greater part of his boyish pranks would be great nonsense. One instance will suffice.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἡ δ᾿ ἐπιθυμία ἐστὶν ἄλογος ὄρεξις, ὑφ᾿ ἣν τάττεται καὶ ταῦτα, σπάνις, μῖσος, φιλονεικία, ὀργή, ἔρως, μῆνις, θυμός.
examples.translation: Desire or craving is irrational appetency, and under it are ranged the following states: want, hatred, contentiousness, anger, love, wrath, resentment.

examples.original: Ὡσαύτως δ᾿ οὐδὲ τὰ πρὸς τὴν γένεσιν·
examples.translation: In like manner the parts concerned with reproduction are not permanent in plants;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ἐνίων δ᾿ οὐδ᾿ ὀπισμὸς ἀλλ᾿ οἷον χυλισμός ἐστιν, ὥσπερ ὅσα κόψαντες ἢ τρίψαντες καὶ ὕδωρ ἐπιχέαντες ἀπηθοῦσι καὶ λαμβάνουσι τὴν ὑπόστασιν·
examples.translation: In some cases there can be no collection of juice, but there is a sort of extraction of it, for instance in the case of plants which are cut down or bruised;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ἐγάμουν δὲ δι᾿ ἁρπαγῆς, οὐ μικρὰς οὐδὲ ἀώρους πρὸς γάμον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀκμαζούσας καὶ πεπείρους.
examples.translation: For their marriages the women were carried off by force, not when they were small and unfit for wedlock, but when they were in full bloom and wholly ripe.
examples.author: Plutarch

definitions: Greek: θέτω σε κίνηση, κάνω κάτι να κινηθεί

examples.original: Ταῦτα δ᾿ οὐκ εἰκός ἐστιν οὕτω γενέσθαι.
examples.translation: But it is not likely that this was so.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἡ δὲ παιδεία μέχρι τῶν ἐνηλίκων διέτεινεν.
examples.translation: The training of the Spartans lasted into the years of full maturity.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἀκούσας ὁ νεανίσκος ᾤχετο σκεψόμενος τίς εἴη·
examples.translation: On hearing this, the young man went to find out who it was.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ἦν μὲν οὖν ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς φιλολάκων·
examples.translation: It is true indeed that he was from the first a philo-Laconian.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Τά τε πάθη καταληπτά. ἔλεγον οὖν αὐτά, οὐκ ἀφ᾿ ὧν γίνεται.
examples.translation: They affirm that mental affections can be known, but not the objects from which they come;
examples.author: Diogenes Laertius

examples.original: Πρᾶγμα δ᾿ αὐτῷ συμπεσεῖν λέγεται πάντων ἀνιαρότατον ἀπὸ τῆς πράξεως ἐκείνης.
examples.translation: This undertaking is said to have involved him in the most vexatious experience of his life.
examples.author: Plutarch

definitions: English: to know; to be acquainted with

examples.original: Πρῶτον ἐκείνους εὑρήσω, χἤξω· τὸ τρίτον οἶδα πάλαι.
examples.translation: I know from experience what the third story will be.
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 12

examples.original: Ἦν δὲ τὸ μὲν εἶδος οὐκ αἰσχρός, ὡς ἔνιοι νομίζουσιν·
examples.translation: In looks he was not, as some suppose, ill-favoured;
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἃ οἶδεν, οἰηθεὶς εἶναι τοτὲ μὲν ἃ οἶδε, τοτὲ δὲ ἃ μή.
examples.translation: By thinking that the things which he knows are sometimes things which he knows and sometimes things which he does not know.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Πατρίοισι δὲ χρεώμενοι νόμοισι ἄλλον οὐδένα ἐπικτῶνται·
examples.translation: They keep the ordinances of their fathers, and add none others to them.
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Τὸ μὲν οὖν πρῶτον οὐδὲν ἠδίκουν, ἀλλ᾿ ἀπῄτουν τὴν ἀδελφήν.
examples.translation: At first, then, they did no harm, but simply demanded back their sister.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἐντεῦθεν οἱ λοχαγοὶ ἡγεῖσθαι ἐκέλευον, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἀντέλεγε.
examples.translation: After that the captains bade him lead on, and no one spoke in opposition.
examples.author: Xenophon

definitions: English: the person there, that person
Greek: δείξουμε κάτι που δεν είναι πολύ κοντά μας, τοπικά ή χρονικά
Greek: εκείνος εκεί (το πρόσωπο ή το πράγμα που βρίσκεται εκεί)

examples.original: Τοῦτο μὲν τοίνυν ἐκείνων πρῶτον ἦν ὧν ἔλεγον.
examples.translation: Now that was the first of the cases of which I spoke.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ἔτι τοίνυν κἀκεῖνο σκέψασθ᾿, ὦ ἄνδρες δικασταί.
examples.translation: Here is another point for your consideration, gentlemen of the jury.
examples.author: Demosthenes

examples.original: Ἀλλ᾿ εἰ κἀκεῖνος ἐσίγησεν, ἡμεῖς οὐ σιωπήσομεν·
examples.translation: But even if he kept silence, I am not going to do so.
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Ἔοικε δὲ τῷ λόγῳ τούτῳ καὶ τὰ δρώμενα μαρτυρεῖν.
examples.translation: Now there seems to be a confirmation of this story in certain ceremonies afterwards established.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ἐπί τε τῶν ὑποθέσεων καὶ τῶν ὑποθετικῶν λόγων.
examples.translation: And the same holds true of hypotheses and hypothetical arguments.
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Σπουδῆς δ᾿ ἄξια καὶ λόγου τὰ περὶ τὴν τῶν βιβλίων κατασκευήν.
examples.translation: But what he did in the establishment of a library deserves warm praise.
examples.author: Plutarch

definitions: English: at least, at any rate

examples.translation: But this, most sapient sir, is not growth, but genesis!
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Γνώμην μὲν οὖν οὐδέτερος εἶχεν ἔν γε τῷ παρόντι διακινδυνεύειν·
examples.translation: Now neither commander had any intention of hazarding an engagement at once.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Συνέφασαν \[οἱ\], καὶ πολλούς γε ἔσεσθαι ἔλεγον τοὺς ἐθελήσοντας.
examples.translation: They assented and said that the volunteers would be many.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Οὕτω μὲν οὖν τότε διεπράχθη·

examples.translation: I Now as for you and me, the relation in which we stand towards each other is really this.

examples.original: Ἐπεὶ δὲ παρεσκευασμένοι οὕτως ἔστησαν, ἐσήμηνεν αὐτοῖς μάχεσθαι.

examples.original: Τὸ δὲ ἔθος ἀρχὴν λαβεῖν φασι τοιαύτην.

examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ὃ μὲν δὴ τοιούτῳ τρόπῳ ἐπάιστος ἐγεγόνεε·

examples.author: Herodotus

examples.translation: It allowed us, for one thing, to catch our breath;

examples.translation: Manure does not suit all alike, nor is the same manure equally good for all.

examples.author: Plutarch

examples.translation: I will tell you if I can.

examples.original: Οἵαν ὕλην καὶ ὑπόθεσιν φεύγεις;
examples.translation: What material, what a field for thy work dost thou forgo!
examples.author: Marcus Aurelius

examples.original: Ἄλλα δὲ ἰδιωτέρως, οἷον ὁ κιττὸς καὶ ἡ συκάμινος·
examples.translation: In some other plants the attachment is peculiar, as in ivy and mulberry;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ἐπεὶ δὲ ᾑρέθη τάχιστα, ἤρχετο πρῶτον ἀπὸ τῶν θεῶν·
examples.translation: Now as soon as he was chosen, his first act was to consult the gods;

examples.translation: And first of methods of planting: as to the seasons, we have already stated at what seasons one should plant.

examples.translation: In the next place, he banished the unnecessary and superfluous arts.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἓν ὧδε πολλοῦ ἄξιον, τὸ μετ᾿ ἀληθείας καὶ δικαιοσύνης εὐμενῆ τοῖς ψεύσταις καὶ ἀδίκοις διαβιοῦν.
examples.translation: One thing on earth is worth much—to live out our lives in truth and justice, and in charity with liars and unjust men.
examples.author: Marcus Aurelius

examples.original: Ἔστι δὲ καὶ τοῖς μετὰ παιδιᾶς εἰρημένοις ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν τεκμήρασθαι τὸν ἐθισμόν.
examples.translation: And even from their jests it is possible to judge of their character.

examples.original: Ὁ μὲν ταῦτ᾿ εἰπὼν παρήλαυνεν·
examples.translation: Thus he spoke and rode past her.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Οἱ μὲν ἄρχοντες τοιαῦτα εἶπον·
examples.translation: Such were the words of the officials;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ταῦτα δὲ εἴπας καὶ ἀνεὶς τὸ τόξον παρέδωκε τοῖσι ἥκουσι.
examples.translation: So speaking he unstrung the bow and gave it to the men who had come.
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Ἔπραξαν δ᾿ αὐτῶν ἕκαστοι τάδε.
examples.translation: The fortunes of the several divisions were as follows.
examples.author: Xenophon

examples.original: Ἐγὼ δ᾿ ἔχω περὶ αὐτῶν γνώμην τήνδε·
examples.translation: But this is my own belief about it.
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Θρῆνοι δὲ καὶ ταφαί σφεων εἰσὶ αἵδε·
examples.translation: They mourn and bury the dead as I will show.
examples.author: Herodotus

definitions: English: as great as, how great
Greek: δηλώνει όλο το πλήθος, την ποσότητα, το μέγεθος κλπ του προσδιοριζόμενου ονόματος
Greek: όσος, τόσο μεγάλος ή μικρός, όσο... (για ποσότητα, χώρο, χρόνο κ.λπ.)

examples.translation: The cause was not so much lack of men as lack of money.
examples.author: Thucydides

examples.translation: He himself halted the rest of the army there, so that they might make what preparations he considered necessary before they were in too close quarters.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.translation: Then, he had tents made for them—in number, as many as there were captains; in size, large enough to accommodate each a company.

examples.original: Τίς ἀγαθός; Τίς πρῶτος ἄνδρα καταβαλεῖ;
examples.translation: Who will be the first to lay low his man?”
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Καὶ εὖ μοι ἐδόκεον λεγειν περὶ τῆς χώρης·
examples.translation: And I think that their account of the country was true.
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Πρὸς ἔκφυσιν δὲ καὶ τὴν ὅλην σπορὰν ἄριστα δοκεῖ τὰ ἑνάενα·
examples.translation: Of the age at which seeds should be sown. For propagation and sowing generally seeds one year old seem to be the best;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Εἰσὶν γάρ, ὦ παῖ, μάλ᾿ εὖ ἄμουσοι·
examples.translation: So they are, my boy, quite without culture.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ἔτι δὲ μᾶλλον ἐφάνη τὸ γινόμενον τοῖς ἐκεῖ παροῦσι νεμεσητόν.
examples.translation: But to those who were on the spot, what happened there seemed still greater matter for wrath and indignation.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Οὐ τὼ σιώ, οὐδ᾿ εἰ μέλλοιμί γε αὐτίκα μάλα κάλλιστός τε καὶ ἰσχυρότατος καὶ τάχιστος ἀνθρώπων ἔσεσθαι·
examples.translation: Megabates, feeling himself slighted, tried no more to kiss him, and Agesilaus approached one of his companions with a request that he would persuade Megabates to show him honour once again.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

definitions: English: one set in authority, judge
Greek: αθάνατο ον, με υπεράνθρωπες δυνάμεις και ιδιότητες που του απονέμεται λατρεία
Greek: ο Θεός, το μεταφυσικό παντοδύναμο ον που σύμφωνα με τις μονοθεϊστικές θρησκευτικές ιδέες δημιούργησε τον κόσμο και τον κυβερνά
entries.etymology: Of uncertain origin; the word is not securely connected to any single Indo-European root.

examples.original: Ἐπεὶ δὲ ᾑρέθη τάχιστα, ἤρχετο πρῶτον ἀπὸ τῶν θεῶν·
examples.translation: Now as soon as he was chosen, his first act was to consult the gods;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ταῦτ᾿ εἰπὼν καὶ προσευξάμενος τοῖς θεοῖς ἐξῆγε τὸ στράτευμα.
examples.translation: When he had said this, he prayed to the gods and led out his army.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Καθέζεται μὲν δὴ ὁ θεὸς ἐν θρόνῳ χρυσοῦ πεποιημένος καὶ ἐλέφαντος·
examples.translation: The god sits on a throne, and he is made of gold and ivory.
examples.author: Pausanias

definitions: English: the other of two; one or the other of two
Greek: ο άλλος, ένας από τους δύο

examples.original: Πάλιν οὖν ἀναστρέψωμεν τὸν λόγον ἑτέρως ἢ ὡς ὀλίγῳ πρόσθεν ἐτύχομεν εἰπόντες.
examples.translation: Now, let us reverse our argument and put it in a different way from that which we have just employed.
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Ἑτέραν δέ τινα συνεψομένην τοῖς κρέασι συνάπτειν εἰς ταὐτὸ καὶ οἷον πηγνύναι·
examples.translation: They say that there is another kind which, if cooked with meat, combines with it and as it were sets it hard;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Οἱ δὲ χαμαιρριφεῖς καλούμενοι τῶν φοινίκων ἕτερόν τι γένος ἐστὶν ὥσπερ ὁμώνυμον·
examples.translation: The dwarf-palm, as it is called, is a distinct kind, having nothing but its name in common with other palms.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ὡς δὲ πρὸς τοῖς ὁρίοις ἐγένοντο, εὐθὺς ὥσπερ εἰώθει ἐθήρα·
examples.translation: When they arrived at the frontier, he at once proceeded to hunt, as he used to do;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ἐνταῦθα δ᾿ αὐτοὺς ὥσπερ ἐξ ὑπαρχῆς μάχεσθαι παρασκευαζομένους ἐπέσχε δεινὸν ἰδεῖν θέαμα καὶ λόγου κρείττων ὄψις.
examples.translation: Here, as they were preparing to renew the battle, they were checked by a sight that was wonderful to behold and a spectacle that passes description.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Τότε μὲν δὴ τοιαῦτα διαλεχθέντες καὶ φιλοφρονηθέντες ὥσπερ εἰκὸς ἐκ συναλλαγῆς, ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὰς ἁρμαμάξας σὺν ταῖς γυναιξὶν ἀπήλαυνον εὐφραινόμενοι.
examples.translation: Then when they had thus conversed and showed their friendly feelings toward one another, as was natural after a reconciliation, they entered their carriages and drove away with their wives, happy.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

entries.etymology: From PIE *nú 'now'; Latin nunc and English 'now' are cognates.

examples.original: Νῦν δὲ πρῶτον μὲν ἡ λοιμώδης ἐνέπεσε φθορὰ καὶ κατενεμήθη τὴν ἀκμάζουσαν ἡλικίαν καὶ δύναμιν·
examples.translation: As it was, in the first place, a pestilential destruction fell upon them and devoured clean the prime of their youth and power.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ὁ μὲν οὖν τῶν ἀγρίων ἀφορισμὸς εἴθ᾿ οὕτως ἢ καὶ ἄλλως ληπτέος, οὐδὲν ἂν ἴσως διενέγκοι πρὸς τὰ νῦν·
examples.translation: So the definition of wild kinds, whether it should be thus made or otherwise, perhaps makes no difference for our present purpose.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ἄνδρες φίλοι, γιγνώσκω μὲν ὅτι νῦν ἔξεστιν ἡμῖν προτέροις τῶν ἀπόντων συμμάχων ἀρίστου τυχεῖν καὶ τοῖς μάλιστα ἐσπουδασμένοις σίτοις καὶ ποτοῖς χρῆσθαι·
examples.translation: But I do not think that it would be of more advantage to us to eat this luncheon than it would to show ourselves thoughtful for our comrades;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Οὕτω δὴ λαβὼν τὸν ἄνδρα ἐξῄει.
examples.translation: So then he took the man and went away.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ὅταν δὲ ἀσθενοῦντα, ἄλλο τι πρῶτον μὲν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ οὐ τὸν αὐτὸν ἔλαβεν;
examples.translation: But when it gets hold of me in illness, in the first place, it really doesn’t get hold of the same man, does it?
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Δεῖ δὲ τοὺς ὅρους οὕτως ἀποδέχεσθαι καὶ λαμβάνειν ὡς τύπῳ καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ πᾶν λεγομένους·
examples.translation: These definitions however must be taken and accepted as applying generally and on the whole. For in the case of some plants it might seem that our definitions overlap;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ταῦτα τὰ ἔθνεα μοῦνα ἱππεύει.
examples.translation: These nations alone are riders;
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Οὐ μόνος ἐμψύχων ἄπεχες χέρας, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡμεῖς·
examples.translation: On the Same Not you alone, Pythagoras, abstained from living things, but we do so likewise;
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 7

examples.original: Κηκίδας δὲ πάντα φέρει τὰ γένη, μόνη δὲ εἰς τὰ δέρματα χρησίμην ἡ ἡμερίς.
examples.translation: All the kinds produce galls, but only hemeris (gall-oak) produces one which is of use for tanning hides.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Οἱ μὲν ἄρχοντες τοιαῦτα εἶπον·
examples.translation: Such were the words of the officials;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ἦν μὲν οὖν ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς φιλολάκων·
examples.translation: It is true indeed that he was from the first a philo-Laconian.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ποιήσας δὲ ταῦτα τἄλλα ἤδη ἤρχετο διοικεῖν.
examples.translation: This done, he began at once to organize the rest of his court.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

definitions: Greek: αυτός και αυτή που ανήκει στην ανθρώπινη φυλή
Greek: ο κάθε ένας και η καθεμιά από τους κατοίκους της γης
entries.etymology: Compound of ἀνήρ 'man' and ὤψ 'face, appearance' is traditionally suggested, though the derivation is disputed.
entries.etymologyNote: The etymology is debated; the compound analysis is conventional rather than certain.

examples.original: Τί δέ; ἄλλῳ ἀνθρώπῳ ἆρ᾿ ὅμοιον καὶ σοὶ φαίνεται ὁτιοῦν;
examples.translation: Well, does anything whatsoever appear the same to any other man as to you?
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Τί οὖν ἐστὶ τὸ ποιοῦν ἀκώλυτον τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ αὐτεξούσιον;
examples.translation: What, then, is it which makes a man free from hindrance and his own master?
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Τούτων δὲ πραχθέντων τοὐναντίον ἐγεγένητο οὗ ἐνόμισαν πάντες ἄνθρωποι ἔσεσθαι.
examples.translation: When these things had taken place, the opposite of what all men believed would happen was brought to pass.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

definitions: Greek: καλός, τίμιος, ειλικρινής, δίκαιος, ευγενής
entries.etymology: Etymology uncertain; the adjective covers beauty, fitness, and nobility.

examples.original: Μεταφυτευόμενα δὲ πάντα καλλίω καὶ μείζω γίνεται·
examples.translation: All herbs grow finer and larger if transplanted;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ἔν γε μὴν ταῖς δοκιμασίαις ἡ μὲν τάξις εἴρηται, μεθ᾿ ἧς ἂν κάλλιστα ἱππάζοιντο.
examples.translation: The formation that would add most to the beauty of the exercises at the inspections has already been explained.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Καὶ τῶν σχημάτων τὸ κάλλιστον σφαῖραν εἶναι τῶν στερεῶν, τῶν δ᾿ ἐπιπέδων κύκλον.
examples.translation: He held that the most beautiful figure is the sphere among solids, and the circle among plane figures.
examples.author: Diogenes Laertius

definitions: Greek: έχω την όρασή μου, βλέπω
irregularForms: The aorist εἶδον and future ὄψομαι are suppletive.
entries.etymology: The etymology is uncertain; the verb is suppleted in several tenses.

examples.original: Ταῦτα μὲν δὴ αὐτὸς ἑώρων ὀρυσσόμενα·
examples.translation: These I saw myself as they were being dug out.
examples.author: Pausanias

examples.original: Ὅμως ἐναργῶς ὁρᾶται πολλοὺς ὠφελοῦσα.
examples.translation: And yet this drug may be clearly seen to do good to numbers of people!
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Ἐνταῦθα δὴ ὥρα ἦν σκοπεῖν πῶς ἔσται ἡ ἄφοδος·
examples.translation: Then it was time to consider how the retreat was to be effected;
examples.author: Xenophon

examples.original: Ὥστ᾿ ἤδη σοι δῆλον, ὡς ἀναγκαία τοῖς αὐξανομένοις ἡ θρέψις.
examples.translation: It will now, therefore, be clear to you that nutrition is a necessity for growing things.
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Ἡ δὲ συκῆ θαμνῶδες μὲν καὶ οὐχ ὑψηλόν, πάχος δ᾿ ἔχον ὥστε καὶ πηχυαῖον εἶναι τὴν περίμετρον·
examples.translation: The ’fig’ is shrubby and not tall, but so thick that the stem is a cubit in circumference.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ὥστ᾿ εἰ καὶ προσέοικε μετάγειν εἰς ἕτερον τόπον ὁ θάνατος, οὐκ ἔστι κακόν·
examples.translation: So, even if it be likely that death transports us into another place, it is not an evil;
examples.author: Plutarch
examples.work: Moralia. A Letter Of Condolence To Apollonius

definitions: Greek: το φρούριο της πόλης, η ακρόπολή της, (με την υπόλοιπη πόλη, στην Αθήνα τουλάχιστον, να αποκαλείται σε παλιότερες εποχές άστυ)
Greek: πόλη, η πόλη κράτος, η πατρίδα, ο τόπος κάποιου
entries.etymology: Etymology debated; the word is not securely derived from a single Indo-European root.

examples.original: Οὐ χρὴ λέοντος σκύμνον ἐν πόλει τρέφειν·
examples.translation: Aeschylus A lion cub should not be reared in the city.
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 10

examples.original: Τοσαῦτά σφισιν ἐς ἐπίδειξιν παρείχετο ἡ πόλις·
examples.translation: Such are the sights that the city had to show.
examples.author: Pausanias

examples.original: Καὶ ὁ μὲν ἔμελλεν ἐγχειρήσειν ταῖς πόλεσι ταύταις·
examples.translation: So he was about to attack these towns;
examples.author: Thucydides

examples.original: Ἔτι δὲ μᾶλλον ἐφάνη τὸ γινόμενον τοῖς ἐκεῖ παροῦσι νεμεσητόν.
examples.translation: But to those who were on the spot, what happened there seemed still greater matter for wrath and indignation.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἔτι μέντοι μᾶλλον οἰόμενος δεῖν ἐπαρκεῖν τῇ τῶν πολλῶν ἀσθενείᾳ, παντὶ λαβεῖν δίκην ὑπὲρ τοῦ κακῶς πεπονθότος ἔδωκε.
examples.translation: If a man was assaulted, and suffered violence or injury, it was the privilege of any one who had the ability and the inclination, to indict the wrong-doer and prosecute him.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Οἰκέτας δὲ πολλοὺς ἐκτᾶτο, τῶν αἰχμαλώτων ὠνούμενος μάλιστα τοὺς μικροὺς καὶ δυναμένους ἔτι τροφὴν καὶ παίδευσιν ὡς σκύλακας ἢ πώλους ἐνεγκεῖν.
examples.translation: He owned many domestics, and usually bought those prisoners of war who were young and still capable of being reared and trained like whelps or colts.
examples.author: Plutarch

entries.etymology: Etymology uncertain; the word is the standard prose term for a living body.

examples.original: Αὕτη μὲν δή σφι ἄρτισις περὶ τὸ σῶμα ἐστί·
examples.translation: Such is the equipment of their persons. I will now speak of their established customs.
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Αἰτία δὲ ἴσως ἡ τοῦ σώματος κρᾶσις πολύθερμος οὖσα καὶ πυρώδης·
examples.translation: Now, the cause of this, perhaps, was the temperament of his body, which was a very warm and fiery one;
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Τῶν ἀγαθῶν ἄρα τρία εἴδη ἐστί· τὰ μὲν ἐν ψυχῇ, τὰ δὲ ἐν σώματι, τὰ δὲ ἐκτός.
examples.translation: Thus there are three kinds of goods: goods of the mind, goods of the body and external goods.
examples.author: Diogenes Laertius

definitions: Greek: χρησμοδοτώ, δίνω χρησμό, διακηρύττω (εγώ, ο θεός)
Greek: ρωτώ το θεό, συμβουλεύομαι, παίρνω χρησμό

examples.original: Θεοσεβέες δὲ περισσῶς ἐόντες μάλιστα πάντων ἀνθρώπων νόμοισι τοιοῖσιδε χρέωνται.
examples.translation: They are beyond measure religious, more than any other nation;
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Τί γὰρ ἂν καὶ λέγειν ἔσχεν ὑπὲρ αἵματος ǁ ἄνθρωπος εἰς μηδὲν τῷ συμφύτῳ θερμῷ χρώμενος;
examples.translation: For what could a man possibly say about blood who had no use for innate heat?
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Οὕτω δὴ καταστησάμενος τὸ αὑτοῦ ἐδίδαξε καὶ τοὺς περὶ αὐτὸν ταύτῃ τῇ καταστάσει χρῆσθαι.
examples.translation: When he had thus organized his own functions in the government, he instructed those about him to follow the same plan of organization.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

definitions: English: bring forth, produce, put forth
Greek: παράγω, γεννώ, κάνω να φυτρώσει, βγάζω γένια, μουστάκια, τρίχες

examples.original: Ἐν δὲ τῇ θαλάττῃ φύεται, καλοῦσι δ᾿ αὐτὰ δάφνην καὶ ἐλάαν.
examples.translation: But there are plants in the sea, which they call ’bay’ and ’olive’ (white mangrove ).
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Δεύτερος ὁ παρὰ τὰς τῶν ἀνθρώπων φύσεις καὶ τὰς ἰδιοσυγκρισίας·
examples.translation: The second mode has reference to the natures and idiosyncrasies of men;
examples.author: Diogenes Laertius

examples.original: Φύσιν μὲν δὴ τῆς μορφῆς καὶ τῆς ψυχῆς τοιαύτην ἔχων διαμνημονεύεται·
examples.translation: Such then were the natural endowments, physical and spiritual, that he is reputed to have had;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ἔπραξαν δ᾿ αὐτῶν ἕκαστοι τάδε.
examples.translation: The fortunes of the several divisions were as follows.
examples.author: Xenophon

examples.original: Ἀφίει δὲ καὶ τὰ ἅρματα καθ᾿ ἕκαστον·
examples.translation: The chariots also he allowed to race by divisions;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Καὶ ταῖς μὲν ὥραις οὕτως ἑκάστων ἡ γένεσις.
examples.translation: Such are the seasons at which each appears;
examples.author: Theophrastus

definitions: Greek: το πόδι σε εκφράσεις ή ορολογία όπως

examples.original: Ἀλλ᾿ αὕτη μὲν ἀπηρτημένη πώς ἐστι τῆς αἰσθήσεως.
examples.translation: But this kind of generation is somehow beyond the ken of our senses.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Πόδας δ᾿ ἄν τις δοκιμάζοι πρῶτον μὲν τοὺς ὄνυχας σκοπῶν·
examples.translation: When testing the feet first look to the hoofs.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Μίσγεται δὲ πρὸς τὴν πόσιν, ὅπως εὐεμὲς ᾖ, τὸ τῆς ἐλλεβορίνης σπέρμα·
examples.translation: (The seed of rupture-wort is mixed with the potion given to promote easy vomiting;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ἅπαντα μὲν οὖν φιλόζωα τὰ κεφαλόρριζα μάλιστα δ᾿ ἡ σκίλλα·
examples.translation: Now all bulbous plants are tenacious of life, but especially squill;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Οὐ τοίνυν ἐκ τούτων μόνον δῆλός ἐσθ᾿ ὅτι χρημάτων ἅπαντ᾿ εἶπεν ἐκεῖνα.
examples.translation: That is not the only proof that he was paid for all that he said.
examples.author: Demosthenes

examples.original: Τὰ δὲ καθ᾿ ὅλου πειρατέον περὶ στεφανωμάτων εἰπεῖν, ὅπως ἅπαν περιληφθῇ τὸ γένος.
examples.translation: Of coronary plants we must endeavour to give a general account, so that the whole class may be included.
examples.author: Theophrastus

entries.etymology: Etymology unknown; the adjective contrasts with ἀγαθός and καλός.

examples.original: Χείρων δὲ καὶ ἡ δρῦς·
examples.translation: The oak also deteriorates from seed;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ὁ δὲ φόβος ἐστὶ προσδοκία κακοῦ.
examples.translation: Terror is a fear which produces fright; shame is fear of disgrace;
examples.author: Diogenes Laertius

examples.original: Περὶ δὲ ἀγαθῶν ἢ κακῶν τοιαῦτα ἔλεγε.
examples.translation: On good and evil he would discourse to this effect.
examples.author: Diogenes Laertius

examples.original: Ἦ ῥά γε ποῦ τὸ φρύαγμα τὸ τηλίκον;
examples.translation: Agathias Scholasticus On a former Magistrate Where, I ask, is that vast insolence?
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 10

examples.original: Τί δέ; ἄλλῳ ἀνθρώπῳ ἆρ᾿ ὅμοιον καὶ σοὶ φαίνεται ὁτιοῦν;
examples.translation: Well, does anything whatsoever appear the same to any other man as to you?
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ὣς ἔφαθ᾿, οἱ δ᾿ ἄρα πάντες ἀκὴν ἐγένοντο σιωπῇ, κηληθμῷ δ᾿ ἔσχοντο κατὰ μέγαρα σκιόεντα.
examples.translation: So he spoke, and they were all hushed in silence, and were spellbound throughout the shadowy halls.
examples.author: Homer

examples.original: Ἀλλὰ μέντοι ἀμφότερά γε κινδυνεύει ὁ λόγος οὐκ ἐάσειν.
examples.translation: And yet the argument is not likely to admit both.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ἡ δὲ τῆς θαψίας ἐμετική· ἐὰν δέ τις κατάσχῃ, καθαίρει καὶ ἄνω καὶ κάτω·
examples.translation: The root of thapsia has emetic properties: and, if one retains it, it purges both upwards and downwards.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ἐπειδὴ δ᾿ εἰς τοὺς δημότας ἐνεγράφης ὁπωσδήποτε, ἐῶ γὰρ τοῦτ᾿, ἐπειδὴ δ᾿ οὖν ἐνεγράφης, εὐθέως τὸ κάλλιστον ἐξελέξω τῶν ἔργων, γραμματεύειν καὶ ὑπηρετεῖν τοῖς ἀρχιδίοις.
examples.translation: After committing all the offences with which you now reproach other people, you were relieved of that employment; and I must say that your subsequent conduct did no discredit to your earlier career.
examples.author: Demosthenes

examples.original: Διαφέρουσι δὲ αὐταὶ καὶ τοῖς χρώμασι·
examples.translation: The cores in themselves also differ in colour;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Xenophon 26. Ταῦτα ἐπιστείλας τῷ κήρυκι ἔπεμψεν αὐτόν.
examples.translation: This message he entrusted to the herald and sent him away.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ταῦτα τοὺς πολλοὺς καὶ φαύλους περὶ αὐτοῦ πεποίηκε λέγοντας.
examples.translation: Thus he represents the multitude and men of low degree as speaking of him.
examples.author: Plutarch

definitions: Greek: χρόνος, χρονική στιγμή, χρονική περίοδος
entries.etymology: Etymology uncertain; the word is already Homeric in the sense of time.

examples.original: Χρόνου δὲ προϊόντος ἀνάπυστα γίνεται τρόπῳ τοιῷδε.
examples.translation: But as time went on the truth came to light, and in such manner as I will show.
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Πασῶν δὲ τῶν ῥιζῶν αἱ μὲν πλείω χρόνον αἱ δὲ ἐλάττω διαμένουσιν.
examples.translation: Of the time for which roots can be kept without losing their virtue.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ἵνα δ᾿ εἰδῆτε σαφῶς ὅτι ταῦθ᾿ οὕτω καὶ διὰ τούτους ἀπόλωλε, τοὺς χρόνους ὑμῖν λογιοῦμαι καθ᾿ οὓς ἐγίγνεθ᾿ ἕκαστα.
examples.translation: To give you the clearest proof that that destruction was effected in this way by the contrivance of these men, I will submit a reckoning of the dates of the several transactions.
examples.author: Demosthenes

examples.original: Xenophon 16. Σαφηνίσαι δὲ βούλομαι καὶ τὴν θρύψιν αὐτῶν.
examples.translation: I should like to explain their effeminacy more in detail.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ὑπατείαν μὲν γὰρ ἔδωκε μετιέναι καὶ παραγγέλλειν τοῖς βουλομένοις·
examples.translation: For he permitted any who wished to enter the lists and sue for the consulship.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Αὖθις δὲ τοὺς ξυμμάχους παρακαλέσαντες ψῆφον ἐβούλοντο ἐπαγαγεῖν εἰ χρὴ πολεμεῖν.
examples.translation: But they wished to summon their allies again and put to them the question whether they should go to war.
examples.author: Thucydides

definitions: English: most, most of all, above all

examples.original: Τῶν δὲ ἄλλων αὐτοῦ πολιτευμάτων ἡ κατὰ τέχνας διανομὴ τοῦ πλήθους μάλιστα θαυμάζεται.
examples.translation: But of all his measures, the one most admired was his distribution of the people into groups according to their trades or arts.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἐπεὶ δὲ μάλιστ᾿ ἢ μόνον περιαιροῦσι τὸν φλοιὸν ἐλάτης πεύκης πίτυος, ταῦτα μὲν τέμνεται τοῦ ἦρος·
examples.translation: But since they strip the bark of hardly any trees except silver-fir fir and pine, these trees are cut in the spring;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Εἶδος μὲν δὴ πώλου οὕτω δοκιμάζοντες μάλιστ᾿ ἂν ἡμῖν δοκοῦσι τυγχάνειν εὔποδος καὶ ἰσχυροῦ καὶ εὐσάρκου καὶ εὐσχήμονος καὶ εὐμεγέθους.
examples.translation: He who applies these tests to a colt’s shape is sure, in my opinion, to get a beast with good feet, strong, muscular, of the right look and the right size.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

definitions: Greek: για να υπερασπιστεί κάποιος κάτι

examples.original: Μέρος δ᾿ ἔσθ᾿ ὅτου ἄλλου ἐστὶν ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἢ τοῦ ὅλου;
examples.translation: But is a part a part of anything in the world but the whole?
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Εἰρήσεται δ᾿ ἐπὶ πλέον ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἐν τῷ μετὰ ταῦτα γράμματι.
examples.translation: This matter, however, will be discussed more fully in the book following this.
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Ὅπερ ἂν οἱ πολλοὶ εἴποιεν, τὸ ἔχειν τι σημεῖον εἰπεῖν ᾧ τῶν ἁπάντων διαφέρει τὸ ἐρωτηθέν.
examples.translation: It is just the definition which most people would give, that knowledge is the ability to tell some characteristic by which the object in question differs from all others.
examples.author: Plato

definitions: Greek: φέρω (καρπούς), παράγω, φέρω, βγάζω κάτι στο σώμα μου

examples.original: Ἡ μὲν οὖν δρῦς τοσαῦτα φέρει παρὰ τὸν καρπόν.
examples.translation: Such are the growths which the oak produces as well as its fruit.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Φέρε δὴ περὶ τῆς ἑστιάσεως καὶ τοῦ ψηφίσματος εἴπω·
examples.translation: Now let me say a word about my entertainment and my decree.
examples.author: Demosthenes

examples.original: Ἡνίκα δ᾿ ἦν ἤδη δείλη, ὥρα ἦν ἀπιέναι τοῖς πολεμίοις·
examples.translation: As soon as it came to be late in the afternoon, it was time for the enemy to withdraw.
examples.author: Xenophon

examples.original: Δρακοντίου δὲ ῥίζα βῆχας ἐν μέλιτι διδομένη παύειν χρησίμη.
examples.translation: The root of edderwort given in milk is useful for stopping a cough.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ὑπατείαν μὲν γὰρ ἔδωκε μετιέναι καὶ παραγγέλλειν τοῖς βουλομένοις·
examples.translation: For he permitted any who wished to enter the lists and sue for the consulship.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Φυλάξομαι· Τεύκρῳ γὰρ οὐχὶ βούλομαι μήνυτρα δοῦναι, τῷ παλαμναίῳ ξένῳ.
examples.translation: And yet there was nothing sure or steadfast in the statements of the informers.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἕτερον δὲ καυλὸν ὀρθὸν ἀφίησιν, ὃν καλοῦσι πτέρνικα·
examples.translation: There is another kind which sends up an erect stem, called the pternix.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Τὸ δὲ καλούμενον κουκιόφορόν ἐστιν ὅμοιον τῷ φοίνικι·
examples.translation: The tree called the doum-palm is like the date-palm;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ἡ τῶν μεγίστων εἰς σοφίαν, οὓς δὴ καλοῦσιν ῥήτοράς τε καὶ δικανικούς.
examples.translation: The profession of those who are greatest in wisdom, who are called orators and lawyers;
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ἐς δὲ τὴν ἀκρόπολίν ἐστιν ἔσοδος μία·
examples.translation: There is but one entry to the Acropolis.
examples.author: Pausanias

examples.original: Τίς ἀγαθός; Τίς πρῶτος ἄνδρα καταβαλεῖ;
examples.translation: Who will be the first to lay low his man?”
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Διαφορὰ δὲ τῶν ἀνθῶν πολλή, περὶ ἧς ἐν τοῖς πρότερον εἴρηται·
examples.translation: There is much difference in the flowers, of which we have spoken already;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Μάλιστα δέ, ὅταν ὡς ἀπίστῳ ἢ ἀχαρίστῳ μέμφῃ, εἰς σεαυτὸν ἐπιστρέφου.
examples.translation: But above all, when thou findest fault with a man for faithlessness and ingratitude, turn thy thoughts to thyself.
examples.author: Marcus Aurelius

examples.original: Ὅταν τις ἁμάρτῃ τι εἰς σέ, εὐθὺς ἐνθυμοῦ, τί ἀγαθὸν ἢ κακὸν ὑπολαβὼν ἥμαρτεν.
examples.translation: Go to and mark what notion of good and evil was his that did the wrong.
examples.author: Marcus Aurelius

examples.original: Ὄρθρου ὅταν δυσόκνως ἐξεγείρῃ, πρόχειρον ἔστω, ὅτι ”ἐπὶ ἀνθρώπου ἔργον ἐγείρομαι·” ἔτι οὖν δυσκολαίνω, εἰ πορεύομαι ἐπὶ τὸ ποιεῖν, ὧν ἕνεκεν γέγονα, καὶ ὧν χάριν προῆγμαι εἰς τὸν κόσμον;
examples.translation: Am I then still peevish that I am going to do that for which I was born and for the sake of which I came into the world?
examples.author: Marcus Aurelius

definitions: Greek: ένα πρόσωπο ή πράγμα στο σύνολό του, χωρίς να εξαιρείται κανένα τμήμα του
Greek: για μια ομάδα στοιχείων στο σύνολό της, χωρίς να εξαιρείται κανένα μέλος της

examples.original: Ὅλως δὲ ἔξεστί σοι μεταδιδάσκειν τὸν πεπλανημένον·
examples.translation: In any case it is in thy power to teach the man that has gone astray the error of his ways.
examples.author: Marcus Aurelius

examples.original: Πρὸς ἔκφυσιν δὲ καὶ τὴν ὅλην σπορὰν ἄριστα δοκεῖ τὰ ἑνάενα·
examples.translation: Of the age at which seeds should be sown. For propagation and sowing generally seeds one year old seem to be the best;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Τῷ μὲν οὖν ὅλῳ γένει πρὸς γένος τοιαῦταί τινές εἰσι διαφοραί.
examples.translation: Such then are the differences as between one whole kind and another.
examples.author: Theophrastus

definitions: English: to be able, strong enough
Greek: μπορώ, είμαι ικανός, δυνατός, έχω τη δύναμη να κάνω

examples.original: Ἐντεῦθεν ἐπορεύοντο ὡς ἐδύναντο τάχιστα.
examples.translation: Then they set out with all possible speed.
examples.author: Xenophon

examples.original: Εἰ τὸ μέλειν δύναταί τι, μερίμνα καὶ μελετω σοι·
examples.translation: Palladas If concern avail aught, take thought and let things concern thee;
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 10

examples.original: Ἦν δὲ αὕτη ἡ στρατηγία οὐδὲν ἄλλο δυναμένη ἀποδρᾶναι ἢ ἀποφυγεῖν·
examples.translation: This plan of campaign meant nothing else than effecting an escape, either by stealth or by speed;
examples.author: Xenophon

entries.etymology: Etymology uncertain; the same stem supplies the adjective φίλος 'dear'.

examples.original: Νέος γὰρ εἶ, ὦ φίλε παῖ·
examples.translation: You are young, my dear boy;
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ὥς γε μὴν καὶ διὰ καρτερίας τὴν πίστιν τοῖς φίλοις διέσῳζον περιφανές·
examples.translation: Furthermore, that it was only by stout endurance that they maintained their fidelity to their friends is clearly manifest;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Οὕτω δὴ οἱ μὲν ἀπελθόντες μεταπεμπόμενοι τοὺς φίλους ἐκόσμουν ταῖς στολαῖς.
examples.translation: So they went away, sent for their friends, and adorned them with the robes.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

definitions: Greek: και· με λειτουργία συνδέσμου συνδέει προτάσεις

examples.original: Dἐπί θ᾿ ὑμῖν εὑρὼν ἀπαγγελέω,φησίν·
examples.translation: If I light upon him, be sure I will report it—says he;
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Οὐ μὰ τὸν Δία, ἦν δ᾿ ἐγώ· οὐ γὰρ οἷός τ᾿ ἦ προσστὰς κατακούειν ὑπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου.
examples.translation: No, in truth, I replied: there was such a crowd that, though I stood quite close, I was unable to catch what was said.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ἦν δὲ καὶ τοῖς συμμάχοις ἐπαχθὴς περιπλέων τε τὰς νήσους καὶ χρηματιζόμενος ἀπ᾿ αὐτῶν·
examples.translation: He made himself hateful to the allies also, by sailing round to the islands and trying to exact money from them.
examples.author: Plutarch

definitions: Greek: δύναμη, δυνατότητα, ικανότητα να κάνω κάτι

examples.original: Περὶ τῆς τοῦ λέγειν δυνάμεως.
examples.translation: Of the faculty of expression.
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Τὸ δυνάμει δὲ διττόν, ἢ καθ᾿ ἕξιν ἢ κατ᾿ ἐνέργειαν·
examples.translation: There are two senses of ”potential,” one answering to a formed state and the other to its exercise in act.
examples.author: Diogenes Laertius

examples.original: Οὕτω μὲν ἐπὶ τῶν μητρῶν ἐναργῶς αἱ δύο φαίνονται δυνάμεις, ἐπὶ δὲ τῆς γαστρὸς ὧδε.
examples.translation: Thus the two faculties are clearly to be seen in the case of the uterus;
examples.author: Galen

definitions: English: bring to light, cause to appear
Greek: λάμπω, ακτινοβολώ, ρίχνω φως, φωτίζω, φέγγω
Greek: εμφανίζομαι και εμφανίζω, φαίνομαι, φανερώνομαι (όπως για την ανατολή ουράνιων σωμάτων και της Ηούς)

examples.original: Ἐντεῦθεν προϊόντων ἐφαίνετο ἴχνη ἵππων καὶ κόπρος.
examples.translation: As they went on from there, they kept seeing tracks of horses and horses’ dung.
examples.author: Xenophon

examples.original: Τί δέ; ἄλλῳ ἀνθρώπῳ ἆρ᾿ ὅμοιον καὶ σοὶ φαίνεται ὁτιοῦν;
examples.translation: Well, does anything whatsoever appear the same to any other man as to you?
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Χρόνῳ δ᾿ ἐκ τῶν ἀπόρων ἐφάνη δή τις ἔξοδος τοῖσι βαρβάροισι·
examples.translation: But at the last in their quandary the foreigners found an entrance;
examples.author: Herodotus

definitions: English: not one, not even one, nobody

examples.original: Ἐπὶ μηδενὶ ἐπαρθῇς ἀλλοτρίῳ προτερήματι.
examples.translation: Be not elated at any excellence which is not your own.
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Ὅταν οὖν τι σῶμα κατὰ μηδὲν ἐξαλλάττηται τῶν προϋπαρχόντων, ἡσυχάζειν αὐτό φαμεν·
examples.translation: When, therefore, such and such a body undergoes no change from its existing state, we say that it is at rest;
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Ἀνίκητος εἶναι δύνασαι, ἐὰν εἰς μηδένα ἀγῶνα καταβαίνῃς, ὃν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐπὶ σοὶ νικῆσαι.
examples.translation: You can be invincible if you never enter a contest in which victory is not under your control.
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Οἱ μὲν δὴ ταῦτ᾿ ἔπραξαν·
examples.translation: So they did as he bade.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ταῦτα μὲν δὴ οἱ ἔφηβοι πράττουσιν.
examples.translation: Such, then, is the occupation of the youths.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ταῦτα οὖν οἱ στρατιῶται ἀνεπύθοντο πραττόμενα.
examples.translation: The soldiers, accordingly, learned by inquiry the matters being carried out.
examples.author: Xenophon

definitions: Greek: παίδες (οικείο, από το αρχαίο παῖδες)
entries.etymology: The etymology is uncertain; the word covers child, slave, and dependent.

examples.original: Εἰσὶν γάρ, ὦ παῖ, μάλ᾿ εὖ ἄμουσοι·
examples.translation: So they are, my boy, quite without culture.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Διδάσκουσι δὲ τοὺς παῖδας καὶ σωφροσύνην·
examples.translation: They teach the boys self-control also;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Τὸ μὲν οὖν ἱππεύειν ἐκ παιδὸς ἦν αὐτῷ ῥᾴδιον·
examples.translation: Caesar, xviii. Horsemanship, moreover, had been easy for him from boyhood;
examples.author: Plutarch

definitions: Greek: αρχαίο πλοίο, το καράβι, το σκάφος

examples.original: Νέος γὰρ εἶ, ὦ φίλε παῖ·
examples.translation: You are young, my dear boy;
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Τελευτίαν αὖ ἐκπέμπουσιν ἐπὶ ταύτας τὰς ναῦς ναύαρχον.
examples.translation: And when the sailors saw that he had come, they were delighted beyond measure.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ἔστι δὲ καὶ ἄλλος ναός· εἰκόνες δὲ περὶ πάντα ἑστήκασιν αὐτόν.
examples.translation: There is also another temple, all round which stand statues.
examples.author: Pausanias

definitions: Greek: μετακινούμαι από έναν τόπο μακρινότερο σε κάποιον κοντινότερο

examples.original: Ἴθι. ἀλλ᾿ ἔρχευ, μὴ μέλλε.
examples.translation: He said ”Go.” But come, don’t delay, they are waiting for you.
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 12

examples.original: Ὁ μὲν δὴ τοιαῦτα ποιήσας καὶ οἴκαδε ἐλθὼν ἔδοξεν ἡδέως ἀναπαύσεσθαι καὶ κατεκλίνη.
examples.translation: Then after he had concluded his rites and come home, he thought he would be glad to rest and so lay down;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Τὸ δὲ ἁπάντων θῶμα μέγιστόν μοι ἐστὶ τῶν ταύτῃ μετά γε αὐτὴν τὴν πόλιν, ἔρχομαι φράσων·
examples.translation: I will now show what seems to me to be the most marvellous thing in the country, next to the city itself.
examples.author: Herodotus

entries.etymology: From PIE *gʷḗn 'woman'; English 'queen' is related through Germanic.

examples.original: Οἱ δὲ οὔ φασι τῇ γυναικὶ ταύτην γενέσθαι τὴν ὄψιν·
examples.translation: Some, however, say that this was not the vision which the woman had;
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἡ μὲν οὖν γυνὴ μετεπέμπετο χρήματα καὶ θεράποντας ἐκ πόλεως·
examples.translation: His wife, accordingly, sent for her goods and servants from the city;
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἐκ τούτων δὴ ὦν σφι τῶν δούλων καὶ τῶν γυναικῶν ἐτράφη νεότης·
examples.translation: So it came about that a younger race grew up, born of these slaves and the women;
examples.author: Herodotus

definitions: Greek: ομηρικός και ποιητικός τύπος της λέξης γῆ / γᾶ: έδαφος, χώμα, πατρίδα, γη

examples.original: Καὶ ὁ μὲν δὴ κατὰ γῆν πόλεμος οὕτως ἐπολεμεῖτο.
examples.translation: As for the war by land, it was being waged in the manner described.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ἔν ποτε παμφαίνοντι μέλαν πτερὸν αἰθέρι νωμῶν σκορπίον ἐκ γαίης εἶδε θορόντα κόραξ, ὃν μάρψων ὤρουσεν·
examples.translation: Archias of Mytilene A raven plying his black wings in the pellucid sky, saw once a scorpion emerging from the ground, and swooped down to catch it;
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 9

examples.original: Καὶ κύων τοῖς ποσὶν ὀρύττουσα καὶ ὀλολυγὼν ᾄδουσα μόνη ἀκρωρίας χειμέριον. γῆς ἔντερα πολλὰ φαινόμενα χειμῶνα σημαίνει.
examples.translation: A bitch digging holes with her paws and a tree-frog croaking alone at early dawn are signs of storm: it indicates storm when a number of the worms called ’the earth’s entrails’ appear.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ὁ δὲ ἑκάστων ἀριθμὸς μῶν ἄλλο τι ἢ Eμέρη ἐστίν;
examples.translation: And is the number of each anything but the parts of each?
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Τῶν δ᾿ ἀειφύλλων ἡ ἀποβολὴ καὶ ἡ αὔανσις κατὰ μέρος·
examples.translation: In those which are evergreen the shedding and withering of leaves take place by degrees;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Τὸ ὅλον ἄρ᾿ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ μερῶν. πᾶν γὰρ ἂν εἴη τὰ πάντα ὂν μέρη.
examples.translation: Then the whole does not consist of parts, for if it consisted of all the parts it would be the all.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ἐτύγχανον δὲ καὶ γένους κοινωνοῦντες ἐξ ἀνεψιῶν ὄντες.
examples.translation: And besides, they were kinsmen, being sons of cousins-german.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Πάλιν οὖν ἀναστρέψωμεν τὸν λόγον ἑτέρως ἢ ὡς ὀλίγῳ πρόσθεν ἐτύχομεν εἰπόντες.
examples.translation: Now, let us reverse our argument and put it in a different way from that which we have just employed.
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Γένη δὲ οὐ ταῦτα μόνον ἀλλὰ πλείω τοῦ καλάμου τυγχάνει φανερὰς ἔχοντα τῇ αἰσθήσει διαφοράς·
examples.translation: But these are not the only kinds of reed; there are several others with distinctive characters which are easily recognised;
examples.author: Theophrastus

definitions: Greek: που έχει αρκετά κοινά χαρακτηριστικά με κάτι άλλο και λίγες διαφορές
Greek: σχήματα με ίσες γωνίες και ανάλογες πλευρές

examples.original: Ἡ δὲ σίδη την μὲν μορφήν ἐστιν ὁμοία τῇ μήκωνι·
examples.translation: The water-lily is in shape like the poppy.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Τὸ δὲ καλούμενον κουκιόφορόν ἐστιν ὅμοιον τῷ φοίνικι·
examples.translation: The tree called the doum-palm is like the date-palm;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ἡ δὲ κόπρος οὔτε πᾶσιν ὁμοίως οὔθ᾿ ἡ αὐτὴ πᾶσιν ἁρμόττει·
examples.translation: Manure does not suit all alike, nor is the same manure equally good for all.
examples.author: Theophrastus

definitions: Greek: αυτός που προκάλεσε ένα γεγονός, αυτός που θεωρείται υπεύθυνος για κάτι κακό (ή καλό) που συνέβη

examples.original: Ἐναργῶς γὰρ ἐνταῦθα τὸ ληρῶδες τῆς αἰτίας ἐλέγχεται.
examples.translation: The hypothesis here becomes clearly refuted by its absurdity.
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Αἴτιον δ᾿ ἦν οὐχ ἡ ὀλιγανθρωπια τοσοῦτον ὅσον ἡ ἀχρηματία.
examples.translation: The cause was not so much lack of men as lack of money.
examples.author: Thucydides

examples.original: Αἰτία δὲ ἴσως ἡ τοῦ σώματος κρᾶσις πολύθερμος οὖσα καὶ πυρώδης·
examples.translation: Now, the cause of this, perhaps, was the temperament of his body, which was a very warm and fiery one;
examples.author: Plutarch

definitions: Greek: (προφέρεται ως μία συλλαβή και γράφεται στο μονοτονικό σύστημα χωρίς τόνο)

examples.original: Πάντα δὲ τὰ τοιαῦτα δοκεῖ καθάπερ δύο γένη ῥιζῶν ἔχειν·
examples.translation: Now all such plants, seem, as it were, to have two kinds of root;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Πρῶτον μὲν τοίνυν χρὴ οὐ μεῖον δυοῖν χαλινοῖν κεκτῆσθαι.
examples.translation: To begin with, you should possess two bits at least.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ἐτέτακτο δὲ ὁ μισθὸς ἐφ᾿ ἑκάστῳ χρησμῷ δραχμὴ καὶ δύ᾿ ὀβολώ.
examples.translation: A price had been fixed for each oracle, a drachma and two obols.
examples.author: Lucian

examples.original: Οὐ φήσω, οἶμαι, τούτῳ γε, τῷ μέντοι ἑτέρῳ.
examples.translation: I shall say, I think, ”Not with that eye, but with the other.”
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ἃ οἶδεν, οἰηθεὶς εἶναι τοτὲ μὲν ἃ οἶδε, τοτὲ δὲ ἃ μή.
examples.translation: By thinking that the things which he knows are sometimes things which he knows and sometimes things which he does not know.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Εἰς γυναῖκα δέ, ὦ φίλε, ἄλλην μὲν οἴει τοῦ τοιούτου, ἄλλην δὲ συγκομιδῆς;
examples.translation: And in the case of a woman, do you think, my friend, that there is one art for the sowing and another for the harvesting?
examples.author: Plato

definitions: Greek: πάντοτε, πάντα (μόνο σε λόγιες εκφράσεις)

examples.original: Καὶ τοὺς ἀμφὶ τὸ στράτευμα δὲ ὑπηρέτας ἰσομοίρους πάντων ἀεὶ ἐποίει·
examples.translation: The quartermasters in the army he always allowed an equal share of everything;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Δεύτερον δέ γε, ᾧ μήτε προστιθοῖτο μήτε ἀφαιροῖτο, τοῦτο μήτε αὐξάνεσθαί ποτε μήτε φθίνειν, ἀεὶ δὲ ἴσον εἶναι.
examples.translation: And secondly, that anything to which nothing is added and from which nothing is subtracted, is neither increased nor diminished, but is always equal.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Καὶ ἐν μὲν ταῖς πορείαις πρὸς τὸ συμπῖπτον ἀεὶ διατάττων ἐπορεύετο, ἐν δὲ τῇ στρατοπεδεύσει ὡς τὰ πολλὰ ὥσπερ εἴρηται κατεχώριζεν.
examples.translation: And so on his marches he always proceeded giving out his orders with a view to existing circumstances; but in camp his arrangements were made, for the most part, as has been described.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ἐπεὶ δὲ ταῦτα ἐρρήθη, ἐπορεύοντο·
examples.translation: When these words were spoken, they advanced.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ταῦτα μὲν τρόπον τὸν εἰρημένον δρῶσιν·
examples.translation: Their ritual, then, is such as I have described.
examples.author: Pausanias

examples.original: Τὰ δὲ κρίνα τῇ μὲν χροιᾷ τὴν εἰρημένην ἔχει διαφοράν.
examples.translation: Krina (lilies) shew the variation in colour which has been already mentioned.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Cἀλλὰ δὴ βελτίονα ἡμῶν αἱρήσεσθε.
examples.translation: You may say you will choose one who is our superior.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Οὐκοῦν ἀπέστημεν αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἃ ἴσμεν ἐποίει ἡμᾶς εἰδότας μὴ εἰδέναι;
examples.translation: But did not we reject that, because it resulted in our knowing and not knowing the things which we know?
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ἅμ᾿ ἡμέρῃ δὲ διαφωσκούσῃ οἱ ἓξ κατὰ συνεθήκαντο παρῆσαν ἐπὶ τῶν ἵππων·
examples.translation: At dawn of day came the six on horseback as they had agreed.
examples.author: Herodotus

definitions: Greek: κατ' εκείνο τον χρόνο, ανάλογο του αναφορικού ὅτε ή ὁπότε, αντίθετο του νῦν
Greek: με αόριστη σημασία· κατά τους χρόνους εκείνους, προηγουμένως

examples.original: Ὡς δ᾿ οὖν ἀπῆλθεν ἐξ ἀγορᾶς τότε, πολὺν μὲν χρόνον ἔκπληξις εἶχε καὶ φρίκη καὶ σιωπὴ πάντας ἐπὶ τοῖς διαπεπραγμένοις·
examples.translation: After Brutus had left the forum at this time, for a long while consternation, horror, and silence prevailed among all who remained, as they thought of what had been done.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἐν δὲ τοῖς ἁρπάζουσι τὰς παρθένους τότε τυχεῖν λέγουσι τῶν οὐκ ἐπιφανῶν τινας ἄγοντας κόρην τῷ τε κάλλει πολὺ καὶ τῷ μεγέθει διαφέρουσαν.
examples.translation: Among those who ravished away the maidens at that time, it chanced, they say, that certain men of meaner sort were dragging along a damsel who far surpassed the rest in beauty and stature;
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Τότε μὲν δὴ τοιαῦτα διαλεχθέντες καὶ φιλοφρονηθέντες ὥσπερ εἰκὸς ἐκ συναλλαγῆς, ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὰς ἁρμαμάξας σὺν ταῖς γυναιξὶν ἀπήλαυνον εὐφραινόμενοι.
examples.translation: Then when they had thus conversed and showed their friendly feelings toward one another, as was natural after a reconciliation, they entered their carriages and drove away with their wives, happy.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

definitions: Greek: μετακινώ, επιτρέπω τη δίοδο της θερμότητας ή του ηλεκτρικού ρεύματος, λειτουργώ ως αγωγός

examples.original: Κατὰ τούτους δὲ μέγας ἦν ἀγών.
examples.translation: But the struggle between them was fierce.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Τί οὖν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τὸ οὕτω συνεχῶς μαντεύεσθαι ἄγει;
examples.translation: What, then, induces us to employ divination so constantly?
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Οὕτω δ᾿ ἐπιστρέψας τοὺς ἄνδρας ἦγεν ἐπὶ τοὺς πολεμίους.
examples.translation: When he had thus disciplined his men, he led them against the enemy.
examples.author: Plutarch

definitions: English: take the initiative in, begin
Greek: έχω υπόσταση, συνιστώ μια οντότητα

examples.original: Οὐκοῦν ὑπὸ μὲν τῆς πόλεως ὑπάρχουσι διῃρημέναι φυλαὶ δέκα.
examples.translation: Now the state has divided the cavalry into ten separate regiments.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Τὰ μὲν οὖν ἐξ ἀρχῆς ὑπάρξαντα καὶ παρὰ τῆς τύχης δωρηθέντα τηλικαῦθ᾿ ἡμῖν τὸ μέγεθός ἐστιν·
examples.translation: So great, then, are the gifts which were ours from the beginning and which fortune has bestowed upon us.
examples.author: Isocrates

examples.original: Ἆρ᾿ οὖν ἄμεινον ἄν τις ἑτέρωθεν ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν μεγίστων τε καὶ κοιλοτάτων ὀργάνων ὑπάρξαιτο τῆς ζητήσεως;
examples.translation: Now, could one begin the enquiry in any better way than with the largest and hollowest organs?
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Εὐλόγως οὖν, ὅτι μηδὲ πέψουσιν ἱκανῶς, οἱ ἐν τῷδε τῷ συμπτώματι γενόμενοι προσδοκῶσιν·
examples.translation: Thus those who are troubled with this symptom expect, with good reason, that they will also be unable to digest adequately;
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Ὅταν εὐτελῶς ἡρμοσμένος ᾖς κατὰ τὸ σῶμα, μὴ καλλωπίζου ἐπὶ τούτῳ μηδ᾿, ἂν ὕδωρ πίνῃς, ἐκ πάσης ἀφορμῆς λέγε, ὅτι ὕδωρ πίνεις.
examples.translation: When you have become adjusted to simple living in regard to your bodily wants, do not preen yourself about the accomplishment;
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Καὶ τὸ μηδὲ ἔμφασίν ποτε ὀργῆς ἢ ἄλλου τινὸς πάθους παρασχεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἅμα μὲν ἀπαθέστατον εἶναι, ἅμα δὲ φιλοστοργότατον·
examples.translation: And never to exhibit any symptom of anger or any other passion, but to be at the same time utterly impervious to all passions and full of natural affection;
examples.author: Marcus Aurelius

definitions: English: hear of, hear tell of
Greek: έχω την αίσθηση της ακοής
Greek: αντιλαμβάνομαι τους ήχους με το αφτί
entries.etymology: The etymology is uncertain; the verb takes the genitive or accusative of the thing heard.

examples.original: Ὃ μὲν ταῦτα ἀκούσας ἀπαλλάσσετο.
examples.translation: With that answer Lampon departed.
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Ἀκούσαντες ταῦτα οἱ σύσκηνοι προσέβλεψαν·
examples.translation: When his messmates heard this, they looked at the man;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ἆρα καί, ὅτι ἐπιτηδεύω τὴν αὐτὴν τέχνην, ἀκήκοας;
examples.translation: And have you also heard that I practise the same art?
examples.author: Plato

definitions: Greek: αναπνοή, ανάσα, πνοή, η ζωή αυτή καθαυτή
Greek: το αθάνατο μέρος της ανθρώπινης ύπαρξης ή το ψυχικό σκέλος της ανθρώπινης ύπαρξης, ο ψυχισμός
entries.etymology: From ψύχω 'breathe, blow'; the noun originally denotes breath and then the life or soul.

examples.original: Ἐγὼ μὲν ὧν αὐτὴ ἡ ψυχὴ καθ᾿ αὑτὴν ἐπορέγεται.
examples.translation: I assign them to the class of notions which the soul grasps by itself directly.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Τί δ᾿, εἰ ποτέρου τὴν ψυχὴν ἐπαινοῖ πρὸς ἀρετήν τε καὶ σοφίαν;
examples.translation: But what if he should praise the soul of one of us for virtue and wisdom?
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Φύσιν μὲν δὴ τῆς μορφῆς καὶ τῆς ψυχῆς τοιαύτην ἔχων διαμνημονεύεται·
examples.translation: Such then were the natural endowments, physical and spiritual, that he is reputed to have had;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Dτὸ δ᾿ ἐστὶν ἀδύνατον γνῶναι, πρὶν ἄν τις ἐπιστήμην ἱκανῶς λάβῃ τί ποτ᾿ ἐστίν.
examples.translation: It is impossible to know the latter until we have adequately comprehended the nature of knowledge.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ἔν ποτε παμφαίνοντι μέλαν πτερὸν αἰθέρι νωμῶν σκορπίον ἐκ γαίης εἶδε θορόντα κόραξ, ὃν μάρψων ὤρουσεν·
examples.translation: Archias of Mytilene A raven plying his black wings in the pellucid sky, saw once a scorpion emerging from the ground, and swooped down to catch it;
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 9

examples.original: Εἰς τὴν τῆς οὕτω συγκαυθείσης μελαίνης χολῆς ἰδέαν καὶ ἡ λεκιθώδης ἐκείνη μεθίσταται πολλάκις, ὅταν καὶ αὐτή ποθ᾿ οἷον ὀπτηθεῖσα τύχῃ πυρώδει θερμασίᾳ.
examples.translation: Now the vitelline bile also may take on the appearance of this combusted black bile, if ever it chance to be roasted, so to say, by fiery heat.
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Μετεκίνησε δὲ καὶ τὴν τάξιν τῶν μηνῶν·
examples.translation: He also changed the order of the months.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Οὐ μὴν ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ τῶν παρόντων ἀναλαμβάνειν ἐπειρᾶτο τὴν πόλιν.
examples.translation: However, as far as circumstances allowed, he endeavoured to restore the city.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Τὰ αὐτὰ δὲ σημαίνει καὶ σελήνη πανσελήνῳ ἀνίσχουσα, ἀσθενέστερα δὲ ὁ μείς.
examples.translation: Moonrise gives similar indications, at the time of full moon: they are less certain when the moon is not full.
examples.author: Theophrastus

definitions: Greek: κάθε αντικείμενο, κάθε τι που μπορούμε να το αντιληφθούμε με τις αισθήσεις μας
Greek: κάθε υλικό αντικείμενο σε αντιδιαστολή με τα ζώα

examples.original: Συμβῆναι δὲ αὐτῷ πρᾶγμα γελοῖον ἱστοροῦσι.
examples.translation: Here, we are told, a ludicrous thing happened to him.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Οὕτως κρίνεται τὰ πράγματα καὶ ἵσταται τῶν κανόνων ἡτοιμασμένων·
examples.translation: And so are matters judged and weighed, if we have the standards ready with which to test them;
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἦν δεκαέτης ὁ παῖς, πρῆγμα ἐς αὐτὸν τοιόνδε γενόμενον ἐξέφηνέ μιν.
examples.translation: Now when the boy was ten years old, it was revealed in some such wise as this who he was.
examples.author: Herodotus

definitions: Greek: που κατάγεται ή είναι δημότης ή κάτοικος της Αθήνας ( Αθηναία)
Greek: Αθηναίος, που προέρχεται από την Αθήνα

examples.original: Ἃ μὲν διώκει τοῦ ψηφίσματος, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι, ταῦτ᾿ ἐστίν.
examples.translation: These are the clauses of the decree against which this prosecution is directed;
examples.author: Demosthenes

entries.etymology: The stem βασιλ- is of uncertain origin; the suffix -εύς marks an agent or role.

examples.original: Οὕτω μὲν τοὺς βασιλέας θάπτουσι·
examples.translation: Such is their way of burying their kings.
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Οὐδὲν γὰρ οὕτως βασιλεῖ προσῆκον ὡς τὸ τῆς δίκης ἔργον.
examples.translation: And surely nothing so befits a king as the work of justice.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἐβουλεύοντο ὡς βασιλέα δικαιότατα στήσονται·
examples.translation: The rest of the seven then consulted what was the justest way of making a king;
examples.author: Herodotus

definitions: Greek: με ήμερο τρόπο, με πραότητα και ηπιότητα
entries.etymology: Related to ἦμαρ 'day'; from PIE *h₂eh₁mer- 'day'.

examples.original: Ὃ μὲν δὴ τετάρτῃ ἡμέρῃ ἐπέπαυτο·
examples.translation: So on the fourth day the storm ceased;
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Ὁ δὲ οὐδὲ προσβλέπει πολλῶν ἑξῆς ἡμερῶν.
examples.translation: But your man does not even look at you for many days on end.
examples.author: Lucian
examples.work: On Salaried Posts In Great Houses

examples.original: Ταύτην μὲν τὴν ἡμέρην παρεσκευάζοντο ἐς τὴν διάβασιν·
examples.translation: All that day they made preparation for the crossing;
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Περὶ τοῦ πάσχειν ἢ πεπονθέναι α΄.
examples.translation: On being or having been affected, one book.
examples.author: Diogenes Laertius

examples.original: Τὰ δὲ νεογενῆ αὐτῶν ὅταν ἁλίσκηται, χαλεπῶς τοῦτο πάσχει·
examples.translation: The young pigs are not to be caught without difficulty.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Δοκεῖ δ᾿ αὐτοῖς ἀρχὰς εἶναι τῶν ὅλων δύο, τὸ ποιοῦν καὶ τὸ πάσχον.
examples.translation: They hold that there are two principles in the universe, the active principle and the passive.
examples.author: Diogenes Laertius

definitions: Greek: έργο, εργασία, δουλειά, βασική ασχολία
Greek: πολεμικός άθλος, πολεμικό κατόρθωμα, πολεμικό γεγονός
entries.etymology: From PIE *wérǵom 'work'; English 'work' and German Werk are cognates.

examples.original: Καὶ τοῦτο μὲν ἔργον τῆς ὀλιγοσιτίας·
examples.translation: This is the main object of their spare diet;
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἄγειν δὲ ἄμεινον τὰς κύνας εἰς τὰ ὄρη πολλάκις, τὰ δὲ ἔργα ἧττον·
examples.translation: It is advisable to take the hounds to the mountains often, but less frequently to cultivated land.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ὅταν ἅπτεσθαί τινος ἔργου μέλλῃς, ὑπομίμνῃσκε σεαυτόν, ὁποῖόν ἐστι τὸ ἔργον.
examples.translation: When you are on the point of putting your hand to some undertaking, remind yourself what the nature of that undertaking is.
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Ἀλλὰ κἀνταῦθα πάλιν αὐτὸν ὁμοία τις ἀπορία διεδέξατο.
examples.translation: But this, again, is succeeded by another similar difficulty.
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Μὴ πάλι μοι μετὰ δόρπον, ὅτ᾿ οὐκέτι γαστέρα πείθω, οὔθατα καὶ χοίρων ἄντα τίθει τεμάχη·
examples.translation: Leonidas Of Alexandria Set not before me after supper, when I can no longer persuade my belly, udders and slices of pork.
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 11

examples.original: Πάλιν οὖν ἀναστρέψωμεν τὸν λόγον ἑτέρως ἢ ὡς ὀλίγῳ πρόσθεν ἐτύχομεν εἰπόντες.
examples.translation: Now, let us reverse our argument and put it in a different way from that which we have just employed.
examples.author: Galen

definitions: Greek: στέκομαι με τα πόδια ενωμένα (όπως οι κούροι)
Greek: προστίθενται, μαζεύονται, συμπίπτουν όλα μαζί, συμπίπτω απλώς, συμφωνώ με κάτι άλλο, ταυτίζομαι

examples.original: Αἰσθάνομαι δὲ πάθος μοι συμβαῖνον ἐναντίον τοῖς ὀλίγῳ πρότερον εἰρημένοις·
examples.translation: I perceive that my feelings are changing to the opposite of those which I described a little while ago.
examples.author: Isocrates

examples.original: Ἀλλὰ δὴ ἔστιν ἐφ᾿ ὧν δεδώκαμεν ὑγιῶς τὰ λήμματα καὶ συμβαίνει τουτὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν·
examples.translation: But of course there are times when we have with sound reasoning granted the premisses, and the inference from them is so-and-so;
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Ὡς δὲ καὶ τῇ ὑστεραίᾳ συνέβαινεν αὐτῷ ταὐτὰ καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ, ἐκάλεσε τοὺς παῖδας·
examples.translation: And when the same thing befell him on the next day and the day after that, he summoned his sons;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Μήτε βαθυκτεάνοιο τύχης κουφίζεο ῥοίζῳ, μήτε σέο γνάμψῃ φροντὶς ἐλευθερίην.
examples.translation: For all thy life is shaken by inconstant breezes and is constantly dragged this way and that;
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 10

examples.original: Δεύτερον δέ γε, ᾧ μήτε προστιθοῖτο μήτε ἀφαιροῖτο, τοῦτο μήτε αὐξάνεσθαί ποτε μήτε φθίνειν, ἀεὶ δὲ ἴσον εἶναι.
examples.translation: And secondly, that anything to which nothing is added and from which nothing is subtracted, is neither increased nor diminished, but is always equal.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Τοιαύτης δὲ τῆς ἀρχῆς γενομένης τοὺς μὲν οὐδὲν συνειδότας ἔκπληξις εἶχε καὶ φρίκη πρὸς τὰ δρώμενα, μήτε φεύγειν μήτε ἀμύνειν, ἀλλὰ μηδὲ φωνὴν ἐκβάλλειν τολμῶντας.
examples.translation: So the affair began, and those who were not privy to the plot were filled with consternation and horror at what was going on;
examples.author: Plutarch

entries.etymology: From PIE *ph₂tḗr 'father'; Latin pater and English 'father' are cognates.

examples.original: Πῶς, ἐμοῦ γε ὄντος; Ὅτι ὃν τὺ καλεῖς πατέρα, οὐκ ἔφη σε εἶναι ἑαυτοῦ.
examples.translation: And time also, which is said to be the truest witness, gave testimony that the god was right;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Οὔ τι ἄν, οἶμαι, ὦ φίλε, εἴπερ γε ὁ πατὴρ τοῦ ἑτέρου μύθου ἔζη, ἀλλὰ πολλὰ ἂν ἤμυνε·
examples.translation: It would not be so, I fancy, my friend, if the father of the first of the two tales were alive; he would have had a good deal to say in its defence.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰς τοῦ πατρὸς προαιρέσεις ἀναμνησθεὶς οἰκεῖον καὶ καλὸν ἕξεις παράδειγμα τῶν ὑπ᾿ ἐμοῦ σοι λεγομένων.
examples.translation: Nay, if you will but recall also your father’s principles, you will have from your own house a noble illustration of what I am telling you.
examples.author: Isocrates

definitions: Greek: που μπορεί να περιγραφεί με αριθμούς λίγο πάνω από τη βάση της αριθμητικής κλίμακας
entries.etymology: Often cited alongside σμικρός; the relation between the two forms is debated.

examples.original: Ἐγὼ δ᾿ ἔτι μικρὰ πρὸς ὑμᾶς εἰπὼν καταβήσομαι.
examples.translation: I have still a few things to say to you before I sit down.
examples.author: Demosthenes

examples.original: Ὅτι δ᾿ ἢ οὐδὲν ἢ παντάπασιν ἀνύσω τι σμικρόν, οὐκ ἀγνοῶ·
examples.translation: I am not, however, unaware that I shall achieve either nothing at all or else very little.
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Τὰ δὲ ἐν ἐλάττοσιν, ὥσπερ ὁ στρύχνος ὁμωνυμίᾳ τινὶ παντελῶς εἰλημμένος·
examples.translation: Others are found in fewer forms, as strykhnos, which is a general name covering plants that are quite distinct;
examples.author: Theophrastus

entries.etymology: From νέμω 'distribute, allot'; a norm is what is allotted or established.

examples.original: Εὐδοκίμησε δὲ κἀν τῷ περὶ διαθηκῶν νόμῳ·
examples.translation: He was highly esteemed also for his law concerning wills.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Ἐπῃνέθη δὲ καὶ διὰ τὸν ταμιευτικὸν νόμον.
examples.translation: He also received praise for his law concerning the public treasury.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Πατρίοισι δὲ χρεώμενοι νόμοισι ἄλλον οὐδένα ἐπικτῶνται·
examples.translation: They keep the ordinances of their fathers, and add none others to them.
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Ἐντεῦθεν ἐπορεύοντο ὡς ἐδύναντο τάχιστα.
examples.translation: Then they set out with all possible speed.
examples.author: Xenophon

examples.original: Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν καὶ τὰ παραπλήσια τούτοις τάχ᾿ ἂν οὐκ ἀλλοτρίως δόξειεν λέγειν·
examples.translation: These and similar remarks may well seem to be not off the point, for the properties of these plants are hurtful;
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ἀλλὰ τὴν ἰτέαν ταχὺ προκαταβάλλειν πρὸ τοῦ τελείως ἁδρῦναι καὶ πέψαι τὸν καρπόν·
examples.translation: But the willow is said to shed its fruit early, before it is completely matured and ripened;
examples.author: Theophrastus

definitions: Greek: θέτω, τοποθετώ, βάζω κάτι κάπου

examples.original: Μὴ γὰρ οὕτω τιθῶμεν, ἀλλ᾿ ὧδε·
examples.translation: Let us, then, not make that assumption, but another;
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Βουλὴν δὲ θέμενοι διεκρίθησαν ἐπὶ τούτοις·
examples.translation: They held a council and settled matters on the following basis.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Οὐκοῦν τοῦτο ἵνα μὴ γένηται, ἕτερον αὐτῶν αὐτὴν ἐθέμεθα;
examples.translation: And it was in order to avoid this that we assumed that it was different from them?
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Τῷ δ᾿ αὐτῷ τρόπῳ καὶ αἱ μῆτραι·
examples.translation: And this also happens in the case of the uterus;
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Ὁ δὲ τρόπος τῆς δείξεώς ἐστι τοιόσδε.
examples.translation: Now the method of demonstration is as follows.
examples.author: Galen

examples.original: Ἡ δ᾿ ἐργασία γίνεται τοῦτον τὸν τρόπον·
examples.translation: The manufacture is carried out in the following manner.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Καὶ ὁ μὲν δὴ κατὰ γῆν πόλεμος οὕτως ἐπολεμεῖτο.
examples.translation: As for the war by land, it was being waged in the manner described.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Σημεῖα δὲ πρὸ τοῦ πολέμου τάδε γενέσθαι λέγεται.
examples.translation: The following signs are said to have been given before the war.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Τοσαῦτα ἐπιθειάσας καθίστη ἐς πόλεμον τὸν στρατόν.
examples.translation: After this appeal to the gods he began hostilities.
examples.author: Thucydides

definitions: Greek: κάνω κάτι να κινηθεί, μετακινώ, σπρώχνω, ανακινώ

examples.original: Οὐκοῦν ἐπειδὴ κινεῖσθαι αὐτὰ δεῖ, τὸ δὲ μὴ κινεῖσθαι μὴ ἐνεῖναι μηδενί, πάντα δὴ πᾶσαν κίνησιν ἀεὶ κινεῖται.
examples.translation: Then since they must be in motion, and since absence of motion must be impossible for anything, all things are always in all kinds of motion.
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ κινεῖν εὐθὺς ἐγνωκὼς τὰ κατὰ τὴν πόλιν, ἔπεισε τοὺς ἐφόρους χρήμασιν ὅπως αὐτῷ ψηφίσωνται στρατείαν.
examples.translation: However, having determined to attempt at once his reforms in the state, Cleomenes bribed the ephors to send him on an expedition.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Οὔτε ἄρα ὁρᾶν προσρητέον τι μᾶλλον ἢ μὴ ὁρᾶν, οὐδέ τιν᾿ ἄλλην αἴσθησιν μᾶλλον ἢ μή, πάντων γε πάντως κινουμένων.
examples.translation: Then we must not speak of seeing more than not-seeing, or of any other perception more than of non-perception, if all things are in all kinds of motion.
examples.author: Plato

definitions: Greek: σύνολο σημείων του επιπέδου ή του χώρου με μια κοινή ιδιότητα

examples.original: Τὰ πρὸ τῶν τόπων α΄.
examples.translation: Preface to Commonplaces, one book.
examples.author: Diogenes Laertius

examples.original: Ὁρμήσασι δὲ πρὸς τὸν συνοικισμὸν αὐτοῖς εὐθὺς ἦν διαφορὰ περὶ τοῦ τόπου.
examples.translation: But when they set out to establish their city, a dispute at once arose concerning the site.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Οὐ μικρὰν δὲ ποιοῦσι διαφορὰν οὐδὲ οἱ τόποι, καίπερ ἔνιοι συνεγγὺς ὄντες·
examples.translation: Again the particular district makes a considerable difference, even as between places which are not far apart;
examples.author: Theophrastus

definitions: English: referring back to a plural subject, and expressing an action done in two directions: of one another, to one another, one another, each other, mutually, reciprocally
Greek: αμοιβαία, ο καθένας για τον άλλον, μεταξύ σας, μόνον στις πλάγιες πτώσεις του πληθυντικού
Greek: για πρόσωπα που ενεργούν με αμοιβαίο τρόπο

examples.original: Τοιαῦτα μὲν δὴ ποιοῦντες ἐγγὺς ἀλλήλων ἐγίγνοντο.
examples.translation: With such tactics the armies were approaching each other;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Χρόνον μὲν οὖν πολὺν ἀντεῖχον οὐκ ἐνδιδόντες ἀλλήλοις·
examples.translation: For a long time they held out, neither side yielding to the other.
examples.author: Thucydides

examples.original: Δεῖ δὲ τὰς μεγίστας αὐτῶν παρ᾿ ἀλλήλας θέντας βουλεύσασθαι, ποτέρας ἡμῖν αἱρετέον ἐστίν.
examples.translation: But we must take the most significant of these ways and, comparing one with the other, decide which is preferable for us.
examples.author: Isocrates

definitions: Greek: σε σύνθετα ή σε εκφράσεις

examples.original: Χρόνον μὲν οὖν τινα ὀλίγον οὕτω πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἠκροβολίσαντο·
examples.translation: For some little time they skirmished thus with one another;
examples.author: Thucydides

examples.original: Ταῦτα μὲν οὖν ὀλίγα πολλῶν ὄντων ἕνεκα δείγματος ἐξενηνόχαμεν.
examples.translation: These few details, then, out of many, I have adduced by way of illustration.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Αἰσθάνομαι δὲ πάθος μοι συμβαῖνον ἐναντίον τοῖς ὀλίγῳ πρότερον εἰρημένοις·
examples.translation: I perceive that my feelings are changing to the opposite of those which I described a little while ago.
examples.author: Isocrates

definitions: English: equal in size, strength, or number
Greek: που έχει τις ίδιες διαστάσεις ή το ίδιο μέγεθος
Greek: που έχει την ίδια ποσότητα

examples.original: ΧΕΙΛΩΝ καὶ ΛΕΙΧΩΝ ἴσα γράμματα.
examples.translation: ΧΕΙΛΩΝ (Chilon) and ΛΕΙΧΩΝ (licking) have the same letters.
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 11

examples.original: Ἀλλὰ τοῦτο μὲν οὐδὲν ἴσως διαφέρει ποτέρως ῥητέον.
examples.translation: But perhaps it does not matter which way this should be put.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Οὐ θέλεις οὖν, καθ᾿ ἃ ἴσος εἶ τοῖς θεοῖς, ἐκεῖ που τίθεσθαι τὸ ἀγαθόν;
examples.translation: Will you not, therefore, set what is for you the good in that wherein you are equal to the gods?
examples.author: Epictetus

examples.original: Fκοινὸν ἀνθρώπων τὸ μὴ πάντα διευτυχεῖν.
examples.translation: It is the common lot of mankind not to enjoy continual good fortune in all things.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Καὶ ταῦτα μὲν δὴ κοινὰ ἀγαθὰ καὶ ἐν εἰρήνῃ καὶ ἐν πολέμῳ·
examples.translation: The blessings that I have enumerated so far were shared by all alike in peace and in war.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Τὰ μὲν δὴ μέχρι τούτου κοινῇ αὐτός τε καὶ ἡ πόλις εὐτύχει·
examples.translation: Up to this time he and his city enjoyed unbroken success;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

definitions: Greek: το νερό, υγρό άχρωμο, άοσμο και άγευστο στη φυσική κατάσταση, που αποτελείται από υδρογόνο και οξυγόνο (χημικός τύπος: H 2 O)

examples.original: Ὕδατος μὲν οὖν ταῦτα λέγεται σημεῖα·
examples.translation: Such then are said to be the signs of rain.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Ὄρνιθες λουόμενοι μὴ ἐν ὕδατι βιοῦντες ὕδωρ ἢ χειμῶνας σημαίνουσι.
examples.translation: It is a sign of rain or storm when birds which are not aquatic take a bath.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Πυρήνης ὕδατα μαρτύρια· οἷσι γὰρ οὐδὲ πέριξ δρυτόμοι ἀπεφαιδρύναντο, λουτρὰ καὶ ἠπείρων ἔσσεται ἀμφοτέρων.
examples.translation: They in which not even the neighbouring wood-cutters washed, shall now be baths for two continents.
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 9

examples.original: Τό τε πεῖθον οὐχ ὑποληπτέον ἀληθὲς ὑπάρχειν.
examples.translation: We must not assume that what convinces us is actually true.
examples.author: Diogenes Laertius

examples.original: Τὸ μὲν τοίνυν τοὺς νέους αὐτῶν ἀναπηδᾶν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἵππους πείθοιμεν ἂν αὐτοὺς μανθάνειν·
examples.translation: We would persuade the young recruits to learn for themselves how to mount from the spring;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Μὴ πάλι μοι μετὰ δόρπον, ὅτ᾿ οὐκέτι γαστέρα πείθω, οὔθατα καὶ χοίρων ἄντα τίθει τεμάχη·
examples.translation: Leonidas Of Alexandria Set not before me after supper, when I can no longer persuade my belly, udders and slices of pork.
examples.author: The Greek Anthology 11

definitions: Greek: που αντιστοιχεί στη θέση υπ' αριθμόν ένα, που δεν έχει άλλον πριν από αυτόν

examples.original: Τίς ἀγαθός; Τίς πρῶτος ἄνδρα καταβαλεῖ;
examples.translation: Who will be the first to lay low his man?”
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ἐπεὶ δὲ ᾑρέθη τάχιστα, ἤρχετο πρῶτον ἀπὸ τῶν θεῶν·
examples.translation: Now as soon as he was chosen, his first act was to consult the gods;
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ἡ δὲ τὰ μὲν πρῶτα ἐσωφρόνεεν καὶ τὴν νοῦσον ἔκρυπτεν·
examples.translation: Atte firste sche was mesurable and hyd hir maladye;
examples.author: Lucian

definitions: English: let come up, give access to
Greek: στέλνω προς τα πάνω, αναπέμπω
Greek: βγάζω από το στομάχι μου, κάνω εμετό

examples.original: Ἄνω, κάτω, κύκλῳ φοραὶ τῶν στοιχείων.
examples.translation: But the motion of virtue is in none of these ways.
examples.author: Marcus Aurelius

examples.original: Ταῦτα δὲ εἴπας καὶ ἀνεὶς τὸ τόξον παρέδωκε τοῖσι ἥκουσι.
examples.translation: So speaking he unstrung the bow and gave it to the men who had come.
examples.author: Herodotus

examples.original: Καὶ οἱ ἄλλοι δὲ λοχαγοὶ συνῆλθον οἱ μὲν σὺν πράγμασιν οἱ δὲ ἄνευ πραγμάτων·
examples.translation: The other company commanders succeeded in getting together, some of them with difficulty, others without any difficulty;
examples.author: Xenophon

definitions: Greek: ό,τι μας επιβάλλεται, χωρίς να μπορούμε να το αποφύγουμε

examples.original: Διὰ τὰς τοιαύτας οὖν ἀνάγκας ὑπελείποντό τινες τῶν στρατιωτῶν·
examples.translation: It was under compulsion of such difficulties that some of the soldiers were falling behind;
examples.author: Xenophon

examples.original: Ἐπέθηκε δὲ καὶ τὴν ἀνυπόστατον ἀνάγκην ἀσκεῖν ἅπασαν πολιτικὴν ἀρετήν.
examples.translation: And he laid on the people the duty of practising the whole virtue of a citizen as a necessity irresistible.
examples.author: Xenophon Of Athens

examples.original: Ὅταν οὖν τοῦθ᾿ ἡ διάνοιά του δρᾷ, οὐ καὶ Eἀνάγκη αὐτὴν ἤτοι ἀμφότερα ἢ τὸ ἕτερον διανοεῖσθαι;
examples.translation: Now when one’s mind does this, does it not necessarily have a thought either of both things together or of one or the other of them?
examples.author: Plato

definitions: Greek: το τοπικό ή χρονικό σημείο από όπου αρχίζει κάτι, η αφετηρία ή η αρχική φάση, το ξεκίνημα
Greek: η πρωταρχική αιτία, η αφορμή
entries.etymology: From ἄρχω 'begin, rule'; the noun means both 'beginning' and 'rule, office'.

examples.original: Ἦν μὲν οὖν ἀπ᾿ ἀρχῆς φιλολάκων·
examples.translation: It is true indeed that he was from the first a philo-Laconian.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Τὸ δὲ ἔθος ἀρχὴν λαβεῖν φασι τοιαύτην.
examples.translation: The origin of the custom is said to have been this.
examples.author: Plutarch

examples.original: Αὗται μὲν ἀρχαί τε ἦσαν καὶ φόρων ἐπιτάξιες.
examples.translation: These were the several governments and appointments of tribute.
examples.author: Herodotus

definitions: Greek: εκφράζει χρονική ακολουθία· μετά, έπειτα
Greek: σύντομα, εντός ολίγου, στη στιγμή, αμέσως

examples.original: Εἶτα ἀμνημονεῖς ἐν τῇ τῶν γραμμάτων μαθήσει κατ᾿ ἀρχὰς σαυτόν τε καὶ τοὺς ἄλλους δρῶντας αὐτά;
examples.translation: Then do you forget that when you began to learn to read you and the others did just that?
examples.author: Plato

examples.original: Ὁ μὲν οὖν τῶν ἀγρίων ἀφορισμὸς εἴθ᾿ οὕτως ἢ καὶ ἄλλως ληπτέος, οὐδὲν ἂν ἴσως διενέγκοι πρὸς τὰ νῦν·
examples.translation: So the definition of wild kinds, whether it should be thus made or otherwise, perhaps makes no difference for our present purpose.
examples.author: Theophrastus

examples.original: Νέα μὲν οὖν ὄντα τῶν ἀρωμάτων ἔνια δυνάμεις μὲν εὐθὺς ἔχει βαρείας καὶ δριμείας, παλαιούμενα δὲ μέχρι τῆς ἀκμῆς γλυκαίνεται, εἶτ᾿ ἀναλύεται πάλιν.
